taxonomy:
## Taxonomy (by core mechanic), using only the provided rules

### A) Illumination / visibility constraints
- **Akari**: Place bulbs so every white cell is illuminated in row/column until black/edge; bulbs can’t illuminate each other; each white cell illuminated.
- **Kurodoko**: Color black cells so each number equals the count of white cells from the number to the nearest black cell or frame (horizontally+vertically); numbered cells stay white; black cells don’t touch orthogonally; all white cells connected.

### B) Black/white (or shaded/unshaded) region formation
- **Choco Banana**: Paint some cells black; orthogonally connected black cells must form rectangles/squares; orthogonally connected white cells must not form rectangles/squares; numbers give size of the area containing the cell.
- **Heyawake**: Rooms (bold rectangle borders) with numbers = count of painted cells; white cells can’t stretch across more than two rooms in a straight line; painted cells can’t connect orthogonally; white cells must not be separated by painted cells.
- **Hitori**: No number repeats in any row/column among white cells; black cells never touch orthogonally; white cells form a continuous network.
- **Juosan**: Fill each cell with “—” or “|”; bold-bordered territories have numbers indicating how many more of one mark they get; “—” and “|” have max extension constraints (horizontal/vertical limits).
- **Kurotto**: Color some cells black; circle number = sum of continuous black cells extending from it (orthogonally); empty circles may have any number; circle cells can’t be colored.
- **LITS**: In each bold area, color four consecutive squares (tetromino); similarly shaped tetrominoes can’t touch except at corners; colored squares form a connected network; no 2×2 or larger all-colored squares.
- **Nurikabe**: Numbers indicate size of continuous white regions; white regions separated by black; black cells form a continuous wall; black cells can’t form 2×2.
- **Nurimeizu**: Shade cells; each outlined region has exactly two blocks of the same number of cells; blocks are orthogonally connected; shaded cells connected across region boundaries; the two blocks in a region can’t touch orthogonally; no 2×2 group entirely shaded.
- **Nuritwin**: (Same family as Nurimeizu but different rule set) Shade some cells; each outlined region has exactly two blocks of the same number of cells; blocks are orthogonally connected; blocks in same region can’t touch orthogonally; no 2×2 all shaded.
- **Shakashaka**: Place black triangles in squares (four kinds); triangles can’t be placed in black squares; uncovered white cells must form a rectangle or square; numbers give count of black triangles around (orthogonally).
- **Sto-stone**: Rooms (bold borders) have a number = count of continuous black cells in that room; rooms with no number any black cells; black cells can’t connect across bold lines; when stones “drop” straight down, stones must fill bottom half with no empty cells (dropped stones may cross/connect across bold lines).
- **Tilepaint**: Bold-bordered tiles are colored; diagonal-line cell number gives count of black cells to the right or downward along that line/column until grid edge or another diagonal-number cell; all cells in a tile are either all colored or all uncolored; final outline forms an object.
- **Usowan**: Fill colored cells; numbered cells can’t be colored; each rectangle bordered by bold lines has exactly one wrong number (wrong colored-cell count); colored cells can’t connect orthogonally; white cells must not be separated by colored cells.

### C) Loop / path drawing (single non-self-crossing loop)
- **Dotchi-Loop**: Draw a single loop through cell centers orthogonally; loop doesn’t cross/branch/revisit cells; must pass all white circles; in each bold-enclosed area, loop either goes straight through all white circles or turns right-angled at all of them; must not pass black circles.
- **Masyu**: Single loop through cell centers; loop doesn’t cross/branch/revisit; passes all black and white circles; white circles require straight-through and a right-angled turn in at least one adjacent cell; black circles require a right-angled turn at the circle and then straight through the next cell on both sides.
- **Nagareru**: Single continuous loop with direction; loop through cell centers orthogonally/turning; doesn’t cross/branch/revisit; must go through arrow cells; arrow direction sets wind direction; wind blocks prevent advancing against wind; when entering a wind cell from the side, must move at least one cell in that direction and cannot hit borders or enter black cells.
- **Mid-loop**: Single loop through cell centers orthogonally; doesn’t cross/branch/revisit; must go through all black circles with each black circle as midpoint of the straight segment passing through it.
- **Moon-or-Sun**: Single loop through cell centers orthogonally/turning; doesn’t cross/branch/revisit; each bold “room” visited exactly once; once left, can’t re-enter; in each room loop goes through all moon cells or all sun cells (not both); after moons in one room, next room entered must be suns, and vice versa.
- **Ripple Effect**: Rooms (bold borders) each contain consecutive numbers starting from 1; if a number duplicates in a row/column, the distance between duplicates must be ≥ that number.
- **Slitherlink**: Connect adjacent dots with vertical/horizontal lines to make a single loop; numbers indicate how many lines surround the cell; empty cells any; loop never crosses or branches.
- **Suraromu**: Single loop through cell centers orthogonally/turning; doesn’t cross/branch/revisit; dotted segments between black cells or outer frame are “Gates”; loop must pass all Gates but each Gate only once; loop starts/returns to open numbered circle; open circle number = number of Gates to go through; black cells at Gate ends indicate when loop crosses that Gate (Gate without number can be crossed any point).
- **Yajilin**: Single loop through cell centers orthogonally/turning; doesn’t cross/branch/revisit; numbers show how many black cells in arrow direction; loop does not pass through black cells or number cells; black cells can’t touch orthogonally.

### D) Non-loop connectivity / pairing / networks
- **Hashiwokakero**: Connect islands (numbered circles) with bridges equal to the island number; max two bridges between two islands; bridges can’t cross islands/other bridges; bridges form a continuous link between all islands.
- **Hebi**: Place numbers in snake parts so 1→5 are sequentially connected in white squares; snakes can’t touch orthogonally; from 2→1 direction, other snakes can’t be in the next squares until black square/edge; black squares show nearest-square count in arrow direction (0 means none).
- **Numberlink**: Connect pairs of same numbers with continuous lines; lines go through cell centers orthogonally/turning; never twice through same cell; lines can’t cross/branch; lines can’t go through number cells.
- **Pencils**: Mark pencils; draw lines from pencil tip through cell centers; pencil is straight group of one or more cells with tip at one end; numbered cell in pencil gives pencil length; line from tip goes through one or as many cells as the number; pencil line can’t cross itself or branch.
- **Satogaeri**: Move circles within bold “countries” so each country contains exactly one circle; circle numbers indicate how many cells it must pass through; some circles without numbers may not move; circles can’t cross tracks of other circles and can’t go over other circles.
- **Yosenabe**: Move all circles orthogonally into gray areas; movement shown by straight arrows (no bending); arrows don’t cross other white circles or other arrows’ lines; arrow tip in a gray cell; number in gray area equals total of numbers of circles entering it; empty gray areas any sum but at least one circle must enter.

### E) Tiling / partitioning into blocks with shape/size rules
- **Chained Block**: Fill black cells; consecutive black cells form blocks; number indicates size of the block containing the cell (or “?” unknown); every block must contain one number or “?”; blocks in corner contact form chains; all blocks part of a chain; chain can’t contain more than one block of the same size/shape (rotation/mirror considered same).
- **Double Choco**: Divide grid into blocks by solid lines over dotted lines; each block contains a pair of white-area and gray-area with same form (rotation/mirror allowed); number indicates number of cells of that color in the block (equals half the block’s total cells); block can contain any number of numbered cells.
- **Evolomino**: Draw squares in some white cells; orthogonally connected group is a block; each block contains exactly one square placed on a pre-drawn arrow; each arrow path passes through at least two blocks; subsequent blocks on an arrow route add one square without rotating/flipping.
- **Five Cells**: Divide grid into blocks of five cells; no blocks with 0–4 or 6+ cells; number in a cell shows how many lines of a block are around it (including outer frame); as many as 5 numbered cells per block; lines must surround a cell and cannot enter a block.
- **Fillomino**: Fill all empty cells with numbers; divide board into blocks; each block filled with same number horizontally or vertically; each block contains as many cells as the number; same-sized blocks can’t touch orthogonally.
- **Hashiwokakero**: (Also connectivity, but fundamentally bridge placement between islands.)
- **Nurimeizu / Nuritwin**: (Also shading/blocks; see B.)
- **Sashigane**: Divide grid into L-shaped blocks one block wide; all blocks must be L-shaped; open circles form the knee (bend); open circle number = number of cells in its block; arrows form one end of block pointing toward knee; number of marks in a block (arrows or open circles) may be 0–3.
- **Shikaku**: Divide grid into rectangles with numbers in cells; each rectangle contains only one number showing number of cells in rectangle.
- **Tilepaint**: (Also coloring; see B.)
- **Tilepaint / Sto-stone / Ripple Effect**: (Partitioning into rooms/tiles; see B/C.)

### F) Sudoku / arithmetic grid constraints
- **Sudoku**: Place numbers 1–9 in each empty cell; each row, column, and each 3×3 bold block contains all numbers 1–9.
- **Nansuke**: Fill blank cells with numbers from a list; numbers are either up-down or left-right; one cell has only one number (digit).
- **Ripple Effect**: (Not Sudoku, but numeric constraints in rooms; see C.)

### G) Snake-like sequential placement (ordered path without loop requirement)
- **Hebi**: Sequentially connect 1(head) to 5(tail) in white squares; snakes can’t touch orthogonally; directional “attack” constraints based on 2→1 view and nearest black square/edge; black squares show nearest-square count in arrow direction.
- **Yajilin / Masyu / Slitherlink / Suraromu / etc.**: (These are loop/path; see C/D.)

### H) “Room” / “territory” numeric constraints (not necessarily loops)
- **Heyawake**: Rooms with numbers = painted cell counts; additional connectivity/stretch constraints.
- **Kurodoko**: Uses nearest black cell/frame counts; also connectivity.
- **Nurimeizu / Nuritwin**: Outlined regions with block-count/size constraints.
- **Ripple Effect**: Rooms contain consecutive numbers starting from 1; duplication distance constraint.
- **Satogaeri**: Bold “countries” each contain exactly one circle; circle pass-through counts.
- **Sto-stone**: Rooms with number = continuous black cells count; plus dropping constraint.

If you want, I can also produce a second taxonomy organized by **output type** (place numbers / draw lines / shade cells / place shapes / connect with bridges) instead of by mechanic.
